clue.text: The first man to make a woman lose her head

indicators.note: losing her head means the woman's word drops its first letter

parts.note: madam is a polite form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: A tale of the first man causing a woman to be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose her head' takes the M off MADAM. The palindrome joke is that Adam's legendary first words to Eve were 'Madam, I'm Adam'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first human created by God.

clue.text: Antipodean saturnalia — should be broken up

indicators.note: a party that should be broken up is one whose letters get split apart and reformed

explanation.surface: An orgy down under ought to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be broken up' rearranges SATURNALIA, letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes someone from the other side of the globe, chiefly from Down Under.

clue.text: Encompassing a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: A bout that surrounds someone.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means surrounding or around, as in a fence set round the house.

clue.text: Sporting a cane and paper can give one an air

indicators.note: sporting suggests playful frolicking, so these words romp into a new order

explanation.surface: Carrying a walking stick and a newspaper makes a person look distinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like wearing, but it signals the anagram of A CANE and PAPER; 'and' only joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or look someone gives off, as in an air of confidence.

clue.text: Pat is in effect a key man

indicators.note: to effect something is to bring it about, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Pat is in fact an important figure in the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in effect' reads as 'really', but 'effect' works on PAT IS IN, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player is a man of keys, playing the ivories.

clue.text: Block cut in points

indicators.note: the trimming word is set in the middle of the compass letters

parts.note: E (east) and SE (south-east) are two compass points
to clip is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: An obstruction is reduced at certain places.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse happens when one body blocks the light of another, so to obscure or overshadow.

clue.text: As is right these days, the team spoke with others

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the current era
a football or cricket team is an eleven, written 11, which looks like II

explanation.surface: Being correct nowadays, the side talked with other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful step is the team: an eleven printed as the figures 11, read as the letters II.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheel spokes are each a radius, so several spokes together form the plural.

clue.text: The racket arousing curiosity about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nosy word goes round the numeral

parts.note: being nosy, poking into others' business, is nosiness
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The din provokes interest in a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arousing curiosity' must be read loosely as the quality of being curious, NOSINESS, which 'about' wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so a state of being loud.

clue.text: The woman uniting the Spanish and the French

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
la is the feminine French for the

explanation.surface: A lady bringing together Spain and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A feminine given name, as in the jazz singer Fitzgerald, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: He's giving up being a plasterer

definitions.meaning: to render is to give up or hand over, so one who does so
to render a wall is to coat it in plaster

explanation.definitionFit: One who hands something over; also a tradesman who coats walls with a cement or plaster layer.

clue.text: Check some proposed additions to new allowances

indicators.note: some of the following words indicates that only a part of them is taken

explanation.surface: Examine certain suggested increases in fresh benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'additionS TO NEW ALLowances'; 'proposed' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or obstruct, holding up progress as a check does.

clue.text: Boring material?

explanation.definitionFit: A drill bores holes; drill is also a hard-wearing cotton cloth.

clue.text: Stormed at for getting into debt

indicators.note: getting into means the small word goes inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
taken as written

explanation.surface: Railed at because of falling into arrears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormed at' looks like the definition, but 'at' is the piece set inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old verb for scolding angrily, raging at them.

clue.text: Bad spirit permissible, it's to be assumed

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A wicked spirit is allowable, one may take it for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoken but understood, taken for granted without stating.

clue.text: Mint small coin fit for a queen

parts.note: a penny is a low-value British coin
royal means befitting a monarch

explanation.surface: A newly struck small coin, worthy of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the coin-making verb, keeping the coin scene going, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of herb in the mint family, once used medicinally.

clue.text: Youngster constantly seen in bar

indicators.note: seen in means the always word appears inside the obstruction word

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always or constantly

explanation.surface: A youth always hanging about in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; here it is LET, an old word for an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare in its first year.

clue.text: Five signify, that's clear

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
to indicate is to signify or show

explanation.surface: Five point out what is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads 'Few', an OCR slip for 'Five', which gives V.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to show them blameless, to exonerate or justify them.

clue.text: Anything but a good-looker!

parts.note: a good-looker is a handsome person; read literally, the opposite of a good look is a malevolent gaze said to bring harm

explanation.definitionFit: A glare believed to cast a curse, the opposite of a kindly look.

clue.text: A toiling eccentric's artistic work

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the words are reshaped oddly

explanation.surface: A hard-working oddball's creative output.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved design sunk into a gem or stone, a form of decorative craft.

clue.text: A tree shelter in place

indicators.note: the first words shelter the next, holding it inside them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree giving cover somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is a racecourse near Liverpool, home of the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: A named locality and racecourse on Merseyside in England.

clue.text: Problems are raised by a scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the words are read from the bottom up

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Difficulties are brought up by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUMS ARE as one run, giving ERA then SMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch humanist Desiderius was a celebrated Renaissance scholar.

clue.text: The craftsman trains a replacement

indicators.note: a replacement puts the letters in new places

explanation.surface: The tradesman coaches a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges TRAINS A; 'a' before it is part of the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker, a maker of crafts.

clue.text: Junior official, a non-drinker and suffering for it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
an ache is a pain or suffering

explanation.surface: A minor functionary gives up alcohol and is in pain because of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior member of an embassy staff, a diplomatic assistant.

clue.text: Note pamphlet put around us is to beguile

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Note pamphlet put around us is to beguile'. D + IS + TRACT gives the answer, but 'put around us' has no reading (TRACT does not go around IS, and 'us' supplies nothing); likely OCR garble, not found online.
annotationWithheld.clue: Note pamphlet put around us is to beguile

clue.text: Strike a leading newsman recorded

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly
an editor, ED, is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Hit a top journalist who was taped.
explanation.definitionFit: Captured on tape, as an audio or video recording.

clue.text: Choose to travel with pro

parts.note: to go is to travel
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Decide to journey along with a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick or opt for something, as in plumping for the fish.

clue.text: Father always appears less inhibited

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for a priest's title Father
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Dad always seems more relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of free: less restricted or constrained.

clue.text: Finding a way around company tax

indicators.note: around means the street letters enclose the company letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Discovering how to get round corporation tax.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT is an old word for a tax or levy, surviving in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical levy or payment, as in getting off without paying.

clue.text: Given credit, a politician must show restraint

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: Once given credit, a member of parliament should exercise self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a clamp or brace that holds things tight, so a restriction.

clue.text: Works to produce a feature with little hesitation in May

indicators.note: in means the feature and hesitation go inside the month

parts.note: the month written as it stands
the chin is a facial feature
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Plants produce something with a short pause in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' as a factory points the surface at production; it is the definition, the moving parts of a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: The works of a clock or engine are its mechanism, its moving parts.

clue.text: A tale of heroes — ill-shod, yes, yet triumphant

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the following words are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A heroic story: poorly shod, yes, yet victorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' rearranges SHOD, YES and YET; 'triumphant' only finishes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem tells of Odysseus and his warriors' long voyage home from Troy.

clue.text: Taking part in a morality play that not written down

indicators.note: taking part in means only a portion of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Acting in a medieval morality play that was never scripted.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, delivered by mouth.
